NAME: The Little Cedar Grove Church
DETAILS: Built in 1812 by Thomas Carter and Thomas Winscott, this is the oldest church building still on its original location in the state! The congregation was originally organized in 1797 by early settlers who first built a log church on the site around 1805 before constructing this  sturdier brick building following the 1811 New Madrid earthquake.

NAME: Battle Point
DETAILS: Located along the Wolf Creek / Adena Trace Trail, Battle Point is one of the highest points in the county. It offers visitors wonderful views of the lake below.

NAME: Glidewell Mound and Trail
DETAILS: Named after Robert Glidewell, a Revolutionary War veteran who purchased land in 1806, the are features a 2,000 year old mound complex built by the Adena or Hopewell Native Americans. Archaeologists have, over the decades, uncovered many human skeletons alongside pottery fragments, arrow points, and copper bracelets mad with copper from the Great Lakes area.

NAME: The Whitewater Canal
DETAILS: The Whitewater Canal, built between 1836 and 1847, spanned 76 miles! It features the only surviving covered wood aqueduct in the United States as well as a still-floating canal boat.

NAME: The Whitewater Valley Railroad
DETAILS: Take a ride on the still-working railroad!

NAME: Historic Oldenburg
DETAILS: Filled with Old World charm, Oldenburg was first settled in 1817 by Catholic German immigrants from Cincinnati. Oldenburg is called the “Village of Spires,” because of its churches, the spires oh which are visible from some distance away.
